subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic final-output sensitive-value sanitization as a core security/config feature, route it to a plugin using outbound hooks, or keep core limited to the current log/tool/transcript redaction boundaries?
rationale: The requested behavior changes visible agent output and security expectations, adds or avoids a new config surface, and can create false positives or missed-surface leaks; source inspection proves the gap but not the intended product boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow core security design
options.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core output sanitizer with schema, docs, tests, and reuse of existing redaction helpers rather than a new parallel engine.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Use `reply_payload_sending` or `message_sending` hooks for an optional sanitizer package if maintainers want core delivery policy to stay lean.

options.title: Limit core to existing redaction boundaries
options.body: Declare logs, transcripts, tool/UI payloads, diagnostics, and selected protocol surfaces as the supported core redaction boundary and close or split final-output requests accordingly.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core security design
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core output sanitizer with schema, docs, tests, and reuse of existing redaction helpers rather than a new parallel engine.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a security boundary and secret-handling policy choice covered by the secops CODEOWNERS routing.
